info.name: roofix
info.description:
Roofix ↔ Phoenix Bridge endpoints. The bridge is an internal FastAPI service on the `ai_shared` Docker network (`roofix:8080`); `ai/roofix/docker-compose.roofix.yml` publishes no host port for it (only roofix-db, at PORT_ROOFIX_DB=5433). Like sandbox-runner it IS exposed through a LiteLLM pass-through: `pass_through_endpoints` in `ai/litellm/litellm_config.yaml` forwards `/v1/roofix` → `http://roofix:8080` (`include_subpath: true`, GET + POST, headers forwarded, `auth: true`), so every request here is also `<litellm>/v1/roofix/<path>` (e.g. `http://localhost:4001/v1/roofix/status`) with a LiteLLM key as a Bearer token — the master key or a proxy-admin key, or a virtual key whose (or whose team's) metadata lists `/v1/roofix` in `allowed_passthrough_routes` (`ai/litellm/LITELLM.md § Pass-through auth`). The requests below use `{{roofix}}`, the direct URL, and send no auth: from your laptop either point `roofix` at `<litellm>/v1/roofix` and add that Bearer header, `docker exec` into another container on ai_shared and curl `http://roofix:8080/...`, or temporarily add a `ports: ["8080:8080"]` block to the `roofix` service. Auth: the bridge itself checks NO token — the pass-through's `auth: true` is the only gate, so never expose `roofix:8080` itself without an auth proxy in front (oauth2-proxy or equivalent).

See `ai/roofix/ROOFIX.md § Endpoints` for the endpoint reference and `ai/roofix/ROOFIX.md § Reanalyzing an email` for the /execute vs /reset decision.

DRY_RUN implications: with `DRY_RUN=true` (the default, and what first deploys ship with), the bridge fetches, parses, decides, forwards escalations, and marks Gmail read/labeled — but skips every Phoenix psycopg2 write. `/tick`, `/execute/{message_id}`, and scheduled ticks all honor this flag. Flip `DRY_RUN=false` in `.env` and restart the container to enable writes. `/status` returns the effective value under `dry_run`.

**Error bodies.** Each endpoint's `#### Schemas` section -- at the end of its first request's description, generated from `roofix.schemas.json` by `scripts/api_schemas.py render` -- documents its request body, its success response and every error status whose body is more than FastAPI's `{"detail": "<message>"}`. Any other error answers that `{"detail": "<message>"}`; a request that fails FastAPI's own validation answers 422 `{"detail": [{"type", "loc", "msg", "input", ...}]}`, one entry per problem.

variable.description: Roofix bridge base URL. Default `http://localhost:8080` assumes you've added a host port mapping to the `roofix` service in `ai/roofix/docker-compose.roofix.yml` (it ships with NO port mapping). From outside ai_shared without one, use LiteLLM's `/v1/roofix` pass-through instead, e.g. `http://localhost:4001/v1/roofix`, with a LiteLLM key as a Bearer token (see the collection description). Inside the `ai_shared` Docker network it's `http://roofix:8080`. From another compose container: `make exec litellm litellm CMD='curl http://roofix:8080/health'`.

Gmail message id for the /execute/{message_id} and /reset/{message_id} requests. This is Gmail's internal id (looks like `18f123456789abcd`), NOT the RFC 822 Message-ID header. Find it via the Gmail API `users.messages.list`, or by looking up a row in the `processed_store` table on roofix-db (the primary key is the Gmail message id). The OAuth token backing the bridge must be able to see the message — 404 otherwise.
Gmail message id for the /execute/{message_id} request.
Gmail message id for the /reset/{message_id} request.
